_schema.subject: server/natural_turn.py NaturalTurn port (mirror: apps/mobile/src/live/naturalTurn.ts). Upstream: github.com/betterup/natural-turn-transcription (MIT), Cooney & Reece 2025, Sci Reports 41598-025-24381-1; decision order from transcription/text.py::determine_utterance_type and _label_turns.
_schema.description: Golden test vectors for classify_utterance (decision order: all-cue -> backchannel; >WORD_MAX words AND >SECOND_MAX seconds -> secondary; first word a NOT_BACKCHANNEL_CUE -> secondary; cue proportion >= PROPORTION -> backchannel; else other) and for label_turns (containment, with the upstream forward-scan `break`) + merge_primaries (same-speaker join across pauses <= MAX_PAUSE_SECONDS=1.5, never broken by an attached non-primary). A Python (server/natural_turn.py) and a TypeScript (apps/mobile/src/live/naturalTurn.ts) port must produce identical results from identical inputs. Language-neutral on purpose: plain field names, timestamps/durations in seconds as floats, `kind` is one of "primary" | "backchannel" | "secondary" | "other", `expected: null` means classify_utterance returns None/null (no words).

classification_cases.text: utterance text as the ASR would emit it (mixed case / punctuation allowed; classify_utterance lowercases and strips punctuation via its own tokenizer)
classification_cases.duration_s: float seconds — the utterance's own duration (end - start), NOT the pause before it

containment_cases.utterances: list of {speaker, start, end, text} fed to label_turns in this order (label_turns sorts by start itself, so input order does not need to be sorted)
containment_cases.expected_labels: labelTurns/label_turns output, in start-sorted order: {speaker, start, end, kind, interjects} — `interjects` is the 0-based index into this SAME sorted list of the primary turn a non-primary utterance interjects, or null for a primary
containment_cases.expected_merged: mergePrimaries/merge_primaries output: {speaker, start, end, text, parts, attached_kinds} — `text` is the merged primaries' texts joined with a single space in merge order; `parts` counts merged primary utterances; `attached_kinds` is the ordered list of `kind` values for non-primary utterances riding on this turn (backchannels/secondaries that interjected any of its parts)

containment_cases.name: contained_backchannel_attached
containment_cases.description: A vocalization fully inside another speaker's span is non-primary, attached to that primary turn; a later utterance by the interjecting speaker that starts after the primary's end is its own primary (upstream containment + join).

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: we went to the lake and it was beautiful

expected_merged.speaker: A
expected_merged.text: we went to the lake and it was beautiful

containment_cases.name: break_stops_forward_scan
containment_cases.description: The upstream inner-loop `break`: an overlapping-but-not-contained utterance ends the scan, so a later utterance that WOULD have been contained in the first primary's span is never even checked against it — it is claimed by whichever primary's scan reaches it first.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: here is my whole story about that

utterances.speaker: B
utterances.text: hang on that is not what i heard

expected_merged.speaker: A
expected_merged.text: here is my whole story about that

expected_merged.speaker: B
expected_merged.text: hang on that is not what i heard

containment_cases.name: pause_merge_within_threshold_new_turn_after
containment_cases.description: No overlap at all here (pure sequential same-speaker utterances) so containment never fires; merge_primaries alone decides: a 1.2 s gap (<= MAX_PAUSE_SECONDS=1.5) joins, a 2.0 s gap starts a new turn.

expected_merged.speaker: A
expected_merged.text: we should talk about the thing from yesterday

containment_cases.name: backchannel_never_breaks_merge
containment_cases.description: An attached backchannel from another speaker never counts against the same-speaker pause gate: the 0.8 s gap between the two A utterances is measured turn-end to turn-start, ignoring B's interjection in between.

utterances.speaker: A
utterances.text: so i told him the plan was off

expected_merged.speaker: A
expected_merged.text: so i told him the plan was off and he took it well
